validity.recommendation: No sheet edit needed. The Diameter_OutOfRange flag is a mechanical false positive in the QC checker itself (scripts/build_qc_workbook.py::check_diameter), not a data defect — recommend the checker be fixed to read DiameterUnits before applying its [2,60] plausibility range, rather than assuming inches unconditionally.
validity.researcher_notes: Pulled the live sheet directly (data/GGIT_gas_snapshot_20260810.csv, header=2): P0906's Diameter='350, 400, 500, 800' and DiameterUnits='mm' — the units column is already correctly set to millimetres, not inches. Reading scripts/build_qc_workbook.py's check_diameter(), it calls N.parse_diameter_set(r['Diameter']) and flags any parsed value outside [2,60], then unconditionally labels the flag detail '{d}in' — it never reads or converts against DiameterUnits, so a perfectly valid 350 mm entry (=13.8in, well inside [2,60]in) gets misreported as '350.0in out of range'. 350 mm is also independently plausible for this system: a prior ref-sweep pass on this same row (batches/india-gas/staging/ref-sweep-operating/rows/P0906.json) found AGCL's company-wide steel-pipe diameter range is documented at 50-800 mm (indiamart.com), which brackets all four of the sheet's recorded values (350/400/500/800mm) even though that pass could not pin the exact four figures to this precise 104.73 km segment (its original citing PDF, assamgas.org/pdf/pipeline.pdf, is now dead — a separate, already-flagged UNRESOLVED sourcing gap, distinct from THIS flag about range-plausibility). This validity entry addresses only the mechanical Diameter_OutOfRange question: the recorded mm values are plausible and the flag is a units-mislabeling bug in the checker, not a sheet problem. Not re-opening the separate Diameter [ref]-sourcing question, which is already tracked elsewhere as UNRESOLVED.
